purpose: SurgicalPlanning is a scripted 3D Slicer module (packaged as the NeurosurgicalPlanning extension) for preoperative neurosurgical planning: MRI/CT registration, skull stripping, tumor and vascular segmentation, and 3D review. It targets neurosurgery researchers and planners who use Slicer.
summary: I found no network, subprocess, pip, eval/exec, pickle, or deserialization calls in the module by search, and no package installation at import or startup. Optional features (HD-BET, Wrap Solidify, Elastix, ANTs) delegate installs to their own extensions and are guarded at runtime. The file is about 24k lines, so I read only the flagged regions. Packaging is minimal and consistent (EXTENSION_DEPENDS NA, build_dependencies empty, CMake installs the one .py and the .ui). The entry tracks the "main" branch rather than a fixed revision, which I note but do not treat as a security defect. No blocking issues found from the inspected parts.

safety.rationale: Searched the whole module for subprocess, pip, urllib, requests, socket, eval, exec, pickle, and os.system; none found. The only file deletion (SurgicalPlanning.py:13511-13516) removes its own temp HD-BET files. No telemetry or data upload was seen. Lines outside the flagged regions were not read.

environment.rationale: No global logging, warnings, sys.path, or environment changes at import. PyTorch is only imported inside the HD-BET run path (lines 13389, 13587), and is provided by the HDBrainExtraction extension. Optional extensions are checked at runtime, not installed.

packaging.rationale: CMakeLists.txt sets EXTENSION_DEPENDS to NA and the catalog build_dependencies is empty, so they match. SurgicalPlanning/CMakeLists.txt installs SurgicalPlanning.py and Resources/UI/SurgicalPlanning.ui. The catalog uses scm_revision main, a moving branch, so the reviewed source is not pinned. A 2 MB banner PNG is committed. The real CMake build and CPack were not verified (docs/EXTENSION_SUBMISSION.md says only a mock configuration was run).

license.rationale: LICENSE and LICENSE.txt both contain the full Apache License 2.0 text, with copyright 2026 Dimitrios Giakoumettis. README.md states the license and no patents. Bundled third-party material was not found; optional dependencies are not redistributed, per DEPENDENCIES.md.

soundness.rationale: The HD-BET cleanup at SurgicalPlanning.py:13511-13516 uses a bare except-pass, which silently swallows errors. The 24k-line single file is hard to maintain. Long HD-BET and Wrap Solidify work runs on the GUI thread with only processEvents. The module does use a parameter node and has guarded optional-dependency paths.

utility.rationale: The README, DEPENDENCIES.md, and a clinical/research disclaimer are present. Documentation says optional workflows are not all retested. No tests or sample data were seen. Tier 1 is declared.

findings.title: Silent exception swallowing during temp-file cleanup
findings.explanation: In the HD-BET finally block, errors from os.remove are caught and discarded, so a failed cleanup of patient-derived temporary NIfTI files in the temp directory goes unreported. This is low-impact, but it hides cleanup failures.
findings.suggestion: Log the exception with logging.warning, or narrow it to OSError.

findings.title: Catalog entry tracks a moving branch instead of a pinned revision
findings.explanation: scm_revision is 'main', so the built extension can change without a catalog update. The reviewed source is therefore not fixed. The policy allows branch references, but a tagged release revision would make the reviewed build reproducible.
findings.suggestion: Pin scm_revision to a tagged release or commit hash for the reviewed baseline (v0.6.84).

findings.title: Real CMake/CPack build not verified by the author
findings.evidence: 1. Perform a **real** CMake extension configuration, build and CPack packaging using an installed matching Slicer SDK/build tree or the Slicer extension build infrastructure. The mock configuration does **not** prove that Slicer can build and package this extension.
findings.explanation: The submission checklist states that only a mock CMake configuration was run, and that a real Slicer-SDK build and package are still required. The entry may therefore fail to build in the index infrastructure.
findings.suggestion: Rely on the index's CI build results for the PR; confirm the build passes before merge.

findings.title: Large single-file module and long GUI-thread operations
findings.explanation: SurgicalPlanning.py is about 24,000 lines in one file. HD-BET and Wrap Solidify run synchronously on the GUI thread, with only processEvents calls for progress. This affects maintainability and responsiveness, not safety.
findings.suggestion: Consider splitting the module and running heavy inference off the GUI thread with progress reporting.

not_checked: Most of SurgicalPlanning.py (about 24k lines) was not read; the review relied on keyword searches and targeted reads.
The HDBrainExtraction extension's setupPythonRequirements behaviour (whether it installs packages or PyTorch) was not inspected.
The scm_url repository at revision main was not fetched; the actual commit and any changes since v0.6.84 were not verified.
The real Slicer build, CPack packaging, and loading in Slicer were not run.
Binary image files (banner, icon, 3D and workflow screenshots) were not inspected.
The remote SurfaceWrapSolidify, SlicerElastix, SlicerANTs, and SlicerVMTK dependencies were not inspected.
